panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of the Salt Range over the Jhelum, storm clouds gathering
panels.action: Raisal and Bhikan Khokhar stand on a crag above the Jhelum, bows in hand and faces set, while a distant Ghurid army winds like a steel snake through the Punjab plain below.

dialogue.text: On the cliffs of the Jhelum, Raisal and Bhikan Khokhar defied Muhammad of Ghor—and left behind not one story, but a tangle of chronicles and legend.

i18n.hi: झेलम की चट्टानों पर रैसल और भिकन खोक्खर ने मुहम्मद गोरी को ललकारा—और पीछे छोड़ गए किस्सों का नहीं, उलझी दास्तानों का जंगल।

panels.shot: wide establishing shot over map-like Punjab, tracing routes between Ghazni, Lahore, and Multan
panels.action: An overhead view shows caravan routes and military roads etched across the Punjab plain, tiny processions moving between Ghazni in the northwest and Lahore to the east, with the Salt Range looming in between.

dialogue.text: In the early 1200s, the power of Muhammad of Ghor flowed through the roads of the Punjab—thin lines of supply binding Ghazni to Lahore and the Ganges plain.

i18n.hi: 1200 के शुरुआती सालों में मुहम्मद गोरी की ताकत पंजाब की सड़कों से बहती थी—पतली रसद रेखाएँ, ग़ज़नी को लाहौर और गंगा से बाँधती हुईं।

panels.shot: medium wide of a busy road near Lahore, caravans and soldiers mingling
panels.action: On a dusty road flanked by fields, traders, horsemen, and mailed soldiers march under Ghurid banners, their faces tired but confident as they pass between watchtowers.

dialogue.text: Victories at Tarain and Chandawar had opened north India, but they also stretched Ghurid power thin, its armies and treasures forever on the move.

i18n.hi: तराइन और चंदावर की जीत से उत्तर भारत खुला, पर ग़ुरी ताकत भी खिंच गई—फौजें और ख़ज़ाने हरदम सफ़र में।

panels.shot: low-angle medium of Raisal and Bhikan watching a distant convoy from a wooded ridge
panels.action: Raisal and Bhikan Khokhar crouch amidst scrub and rock, their eyes narrowed as they watch a distant Ghurid convoy snake along the valley floor under fluttering standards.

dialogue.text: In the hills above these roads lived the Khokhars—tribal chiefs of the Salt Range, fierce horsemen and raiders who had long guarded and taxed the passes.

i18n.hi: इन सड़कों के ऊपर की पहाड़ियों में बसते थे खोक्खर—साल्ट रेंज के कबायली सरदार, घोड़ेसवार हमलावर, जो सदियों से दरों की रखवाली और वसूली करते आए थे।

panels.shot: tight medium on a Khokhar council circle by firelight
panels.action: By a night fire in a mountain encampment, Raisal and Bhikan sit among weathered Khokhar elders, faces lit by flames as they gesture toward the lowlands and the imagined line of the road.

dialogue.speaker: Bhikan
dialogue.text: They take our hills for their road. Let them learn these hills bite.

i18n.hi: हमारी पहाड़ियों को अपनी सड़क समझते हैं? चलो सिखाएँ, ये पहाड़ काटते भी हैं।

panels.shot: dynamic wide of an ambush in a narrow defile, viewed from above
panels.action: In a steep, rocky gorge, Khokhar warriors surge down from the sides, bows and spears raised, as a startled Ghurid caravan halts amid rearing horses and toppled pack animals.

dialogue.text: Around 1204, the chronicles say, the Khokhars rose. They blocked the passes, struck at caravans, and cut the veins that fed Lahore and Ghazni.

i18n.hi: क़रीब 1204 में, लिहाज़ बताते हैं, खोक्खर उठ खड़े हुए। उन्होंने दरें रोकीं, काफिलों पर धावा बोला, और लाहौर–ग़ज़नी की साँसें काट दीं।

panels.shot: close-up on a Ghurid messenger spurring his horse, dust flying
panels.action: A Ghurid rider, cloak streaming, leans low over his galloping horse as he races along a rutted track, the outline of Lahore’s walls faint in the distance.

dialogue.text: In Lahore, word came like a wound. Muhammad’s lieutenants sent urgent messages west: the Punjab roads were no longer safe.

i18n.hi: लाहौर में खबर घाव की तरह लगी। मुहम्मद के अमीरों ने जल्दी-जल्दी पैगाम पश्चिम भेजे: पंजाब की राहें अब महफ़ूज़ नहीं रहीं।

panels.shot: regal interior medium of Muhammad of Ghor seated in council in Ghazni (Muhammad unseen, implied by throne and courtiers)
panels.action: Inside a richly decorated hall in Ghazni, turbaned amirs and scribes bend over a map of the Punjab spread before a raised empty throne, their fingers tracing the Jhelum and the jagged line of the Salt Range.

dialogue.text: Far to the west, in Ghazni, Muhammad of Ghor listened. To lose the Punjab roads was to lose the bridge to his Indian conquests.

i18n.hi: दूर पश्चिम, ग़ज़नी में मुहम्मद गोरी ने सुना। पंजाब की राहें खोना, हिन्दुस्तानी फतह का पुल खोना था।

panels.shot: long shot of a Ghurid army column leaving Ghazni, mountains in background
panels.action: An ordered Ghurid army marches out of Ghazni’s gate beneath high walls and snowy peaks, banners snapping in the wind as ranks of cavalry and infantry move toward the hazy east.

dialogue.text: So he came in person. The sources agree: in 1206, Muhammad marched east against the Khokhar revolt on the Jhelum.

i18n.hi: तो वो ख़ुद चला। सारे ज़रिए मानते हैं: 1206 में मुहम्मद झेलम पर खोक्खर बगावत कुचलने पूरब कूच पर निकला।

panels.shot: wide shot of opposing forces facing off near the Jhelum, river glinting between them
panels.action: On one side of the glinting Jhelum, rows of Ghurid troops stand in disciplined ranks; on the rising ground opposite, scattered but fierce Khokhar bands cluster under their chiefs, with Raisal and Bhikan at the forefront.

dialogue.text: On the banks of the Jhelum, the two worlds met—organized imperial host below, hill fighters above, each testing who truly held the passage.

i18n.hi: झेलम के किनारे दो जहाँ टकराए—नीचे सजधज के साथ सल्तनती लश्कर, ऊपर पहाड़ी जंगजू, दोनों आज़मा रहे थे असल में राह किसकी है।

panels.shot: medium close on Raisal drawing his bow, grim focus
panels.action: Raisal, jaw set, draws a taut bowstring as arrows arc from Khokhar lines toward the advancing Ghurid foot, while Bhikan rallies riders behind him for a downhill charge.

dialogue.speaker: Raisal
dialogue.text: For every pass they take, we take a man.

i18n.hi: हर दर वो लें, हम एक जान लें।

panels.shot: chaotic mid-wide of the battlefield, dust and confusion, no graphic violence
panels.action: Dust clouds blur the clash as cavalry surge, shields lock, and men struggle in a haze of movement, the Jhelum and the rocky hills looming behind the melee.

dialogue.text: The chroniclers give no neat numbers, only hard words: a revolt, bitter fighting, then a crushing of the Khokhars by the sultan’s army.

i18n.hi: इतिहासियों ने गिनती नहीं, बस कड़वे लफ़्ज़ दिए: बगावत, खूँख़ार जंग, और फिर सुल्तानी फौज के हाथों खोक्खरों की सख़्त कुचलाई।

panels.shot: somber wide of a subdued Khokhar encampment under Ghurid guard
panels.action: Khokhar men, women and children sit grouped and guarded in a valley camp, surrounded by Ghurid soldiers; some elders stare defiant, others look hollow as the soldiers stand watch.

dialogue.text: Minhaj and Ibn al-Athir record the aftermath: many Khokhars killed, others taken as captives, with talk of forced conversion and enslavement in the Persian tradition.

i18n.hi: मिनहाज और इब्नुल असीर अंजाम लिखते हैं: कई खोक्खर मारे गए, कई क़ैद हुए, और ज़बरन इस्लाम और गुलामी की फ़ारसी रिवायत का ज़िक्र हुआ।

panels.shot: close-up on a Ghurid officer dictating to a scribe, scroll partially unrolled
panels.action: A Ghurid officer, armored and severe, leans toward a seated scribe who writes quickly on a scroll, the officer’s hand emphasizing words as he recounts the campaign.

dialogue.text: These accounts were written from the victors’ halls, but they agree: the revolt was broken by heavy, punitive violence.

i18n.hi: ये बयान फ़तहयाफ़्ता दरबारों से लिखे गए, पर सब मानते हैं: बगावत भारी, सज़ागार हिंसा से तोड़ी गई।

panels.shot: medium of Muhammad’s camp at Dhamiak by night, tents around a central pavilion
panels.action: By night in a valley near the Salt Range, a ring of tents stands around a larger pavilion, small lamps glowing as guards with spears pace the perimeter beneath a starry sky.

dialogue.text: With the roads reopened, Muhammad of Ghor turned homeward. At a place called Dhamiak, near the Salt Range, he camped for the night.

i18n.hi: रास्ते फिर खुलते ही मुहम्मद गोरी ने रुख वतन को मोड़ा। साल्ट रेंज के पास धामियाक नाम जगह पर उसने डेरा डाला।

panels.shot: tense close-up on a shadowed figure entering the royal pavilion flap
panels.action: A shadowed figure, face obscured by a hood, parts the flap of the central pavilion, slipping inside as two drowsy sentries stand nearby in the dim light.

dialogue.text: Then the chronicles fall into shadow. Minhaj and Ibn al-Athir relate that assassins stole into the sultan’s tent at Dhamiak.

i18n.hi: फिर तवारीख़ धुंधली हो जाती हैं। मिनहाज और इब्नुल असीर लिखते हैं कि धामियाक में क़ातिल चुपके से सुल्तान के ख़ेमे में घुस आए।

panels.shot: interior silhouette shot of confusion in the pavilion, lamp overturned
panels.action: Inside the pavilion, seen in silhouette, figures struggle briefly; a lamp topples, throwing the scene into deeper darkness as attendants rush forward in alarm.

dialogue.text: They name them Ismaili or Batini killers, part of a wider web of secret foes that stalked rulers from Iran to India.

i18n.hi: वो उन्हें इस्माइली या बातिनी हत्यारे कहते हैं—एक गुप्त जाल का हिस्सा, जो ईरान से हिन्द तक बादशाहों का पीछा करता था।

panels.shot: wide dawn shot of the camp in disarray, banners lowered
panels.action: At dawn, the Dhamiak camp lies unsettled; soldiers cluster in murmur, banners hang slack, and the central pavilion stands still as the first light touches the Salt Range ridges.

dialogue.text: By morning, Muhammad of Ghor was dead. The road-clearing conqueror of the Khokhars would never return to Ghazni or Delhi.

i18n.hi: सुबह तक मुहम्मद गोरी मर चुका था। खोक्खरों का रास्ता साफ़ करने वाला फ़ातह न फिर ग़ज़नी लौटा, न दिल्ली।

panels.shot: split-scene style wide: on one side a Persian court historian writing; on the other, Khokhar warriors around a hill fire
panels.action: On one half, a Persian court historian sits in a lamp-lit study, writing intently; on the other, Khokhar warriors huddle around a mountain fire, an elder gesturing as he tells a tale.

dialogue.text: Later, Ferishta would echo a different voice—that the Khokhars, not hidden sectaries, avenged their dead upon their conqueror.

i18n.hi: बाद में फ़रिश्ता ने दूसरी आवाज़ दोहराई—कि ये छुपे फ़िरक़े नहीं, खुद खोक्खर थे, जिन्होंने अपने क़ातिल फ़तहयाब से बदला लिया।

panels.shot: medium close on an open manuscript showing two marginal notes in different hands
panels.action: An aged manuscript lies open, its main text in neat script, while two different hands have added marginal notes that point to the same event but name different killers.

dialogue.text: Modern historians note the pattern: agreement on the revolt, its brutal suppression, and the sultan’s death—disagreement on who dealt the final blow.

i18n.hi: आज के इतिहासकार धारा देख पाते हैं: बगावत पर इत्तिफ़ाक, उसकी बेरहम कुचलन पर इत्तिफ़ाक, और सुल्तान की मौत पर भी—मतभेद बस इस पर कि आख़िरी वार किसने किया।

panels.shot: wide contemplative shot of Raisal and Bhikan’s silhouettes against the Salt Range, years later feel
panels.action: Silhouetted atop a rugged ridge, figures evoking Raisal and Bhikan stand against the vast Salt Range and the winding Jhelum below, as if suspended between legend and record.

dialogue.text: Between the Khokhar hills and the Dhamiak plain, we are left with roads, ruins, and rival chronicles—a reminder that in history, the battle is only half the story, the sources the other half.

i18n.hi: खोक्खर की पहाड़ियों और धामियाक के मैदानी दरम्यान हमारे पास बस सड़कें, खंडहर और टकराती तवारीख़ बचती हैं—याद दिलाती हुईं कि जंग आधी कहानी है, आधे किस्से तो उन सरगोशियों में हैं जो उन्हें लिखते हैं।

title_i18n.en: The Khokhars Rise on the Jhelum
